name: Small Shadow Gaps Admit Exact Relative Peelings
statement: Let $\varnothing\ne B\subseteq A\subseteq Q_F$ be ample, and suppose every support in $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ has size at most two. Then $A$ reduces to $B$ by deleting corners of degree at most two while retaining every concept of $B$. Equivalently, starting from $B$ and repeatedly adding an outside concept with the largest current number of neighbors always preserves ampleness and reaches $A$, acquiring a support of size at most two at each step. For every $T\subseteq B$, including $T=\varnothing$, $A$ reduces to $T$ by corner deletions exactly when $B$ does. Hence $A$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $B$ is, and $A$ peels to any $b\in B$ exactly when $B$ does. If $A$ and $B$ have the same active coordinates, every relative deletion has degree exactly two.
proof: Every cube of $A$ of dimension at least three lies in $B$: extend it to a maximal cube, use connectedness of the corresponding reduction to see that it is the unique cube of its support, and then use ampleness of $B$ to locate that same cube there. The same uniqueness holds for maximal squares. For an ample intermediate $B\subseteq S\subsetneq A$, choose an outside concept $x$ with the most neighbors in $S$. Its punctured incident cube lies in $S$, so it has at most two directions. With two directions, maximal-square uniqueness shows the pair is not already shattered and the one-concept criterion preserves ampleness. With one direction, maximality makes $S$ locally convex and hence convex; that direction is constant on $S$, so it is again newly acquired. Iteration gives the relative order. Rank-at-most-two extension invariance preserves reduction to every retained target $T$. Equal active coordinate sets rule out a one-direction step.
